stories.text: Votes are being counted in the US midterm elections, and early results point to gains for the Democrats.
Foreign Secretary Miliband says a UK apology for slavery will not cost taxpayers, adding that Britain cannot hide from its past.
Some GP surgeries will soon offer multi-cancer blood tests, aiming to catch liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancers much earlier.
A Poundland supplier says it will lose millions if the retailer collapses, while other suppliers warn they would go out of business.
Scammers are using AI-generated pictures of missing pets to demand reward money, with some owners threatened that their cats would be killed.
Kellogg's is dropping rice grains from Rice Krispies because of changing weather, and packs will now carry a wheat gluten warning.
Spain's transport minister has resigned days after a train collision south of Madrid killed at least 69 people and injured dozens.
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been summonsed to give evidence in December at a businessman's fraud trial in the High Court.
Kim Kardashian explains her return for a second series of the drama All's Fair, saying she has worked on her acting.
The code of a brass padlock found near Port Talbot, part of a treasure hoard from a 1583 shipwreck, has been cracked.
